title: VPC connectivity — concept map
intro: Once your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) exists, you connect it to AWS services, other VPCs, and on-premises networks. Gateway and Interface VPC endpoints keep API traffic private. VPC peering links two VPCs but is not transitive. Transit Gateway (TGW) scales hub-and-spoke. Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect bring hybrid traffic in. AWS PrivateLink exposes SaaS without peering. The hybrid walkthrough ties it together.

conceptCards.title: VPC endpoints
conceptCards.summary: Gateway for S3/DynamoDB via route tables. Interface ENIs for other services with SG + optional private DNS.
conceptCards.example: S3 Gateway endpoint removes NAT for artifact pulls

conceptCards.title: VPC peering
conceptCards.summary: One-to-one L3 link. Not transitive. Non-overlapping CIDR. Routes both ways + SG/NACL.

conceptCards.title: Transit Gateway
conceptCards.summary: Regional hub with route tables. Transitive within design. Attach VPC, VPN, DX.
conceptCards.example: On-prem via DX → TGW → 12 VPC spokes

conceptCards.title: VPN & Direct Connect
conceptCards.summary: VPN = IPsec over internet with dual tunnels. DX = private circuit. BGP for routes.
conceptCards.example: DX primary + VPN backup to same TGW

conceptCards.title: PrivateLink
conceptCards.summary: Provider NLB + endpoint service. Consumer Interface endpoint. No full VPC peering.
conceptCards.example: Fraud SaaS API via vpce-svc DNS

conceptCards.title: Hybrid walkthrough
conceptCards.summary: DX+VPN → TGW segmentation → endpoints per VPC → PrivateLink SaaS → failover drill.
conceptCards.example: ERP on-prem batch sync to prod VPC over DX
